subject: Invoice 2026-04: staging traffic counted as production / VAT treatment question
messages:
From: Samantha Green <samantha.green@cartwheel.ai>

Cc: Billing Team <billing@cartwheel.ai>
Date: 2026-04-26T09:32:00Z
Subject: Invoice 2026-04 — large dev/staging usage included

Hi Marissa,

We received invoice Redwood-2026-04 for April and noticed a ~350k token line item that looks like traffic from our staging cluster (staging.cartwheel.ai) between 2026-04-14 and 2026-04-16. We have a migration that ran over the weekend and several integration tests hit the API. Per our contract we expected staging to be excluded for our reserved capacity plan.

Can you confirm whether the usage shown on line 4 (tokenized requests 2026-04-14 01:00 — 2026-04-16 23:59 UTC) is being billed to our production org or if this is an attribution error? We would like to place payment on hold for that portion of the invoice until resolved.

I attached a small CSV extract from our side with matching request ids and timestamps. Also, quick VAT question: we are Cartwheel GmbH (DE) — should Redwood apply EU VAT on this invoice or reverse charge to our VAT number? We’ve included our VAT id in the attachment header.

Thanks,
Samantha Green
Head of Engineering Operations
Cartwheel GmbH

Subject: Re: Invoice 2026-04 — large dev/staging usage included

Thanks Samantha — sorry about the surprise. I’ve looped in Lauren from Billing and Ben from Sales to expedite.

Quick notes:
- We’ll pull a token-level export for the period you cite and compare request ids/timestamps to your CSV.
- If traffic is indeed tagged to a staging hostname or has a sandbox API key, we’ll isolate it and propose a retroactive credit for the affected tokens.
- On VAT: our default behavior is to charge VAT for EU customers if the invoice is issued to a local entity, but we’ll validate against the VAT number you provided and the contract. If reverse-charge applies, we’ll reissue.

Can you share the account org id (the internal Cartwheel org GUID) and a couple more request ids (full UUIDs) from the period? Lauren will need them to map logs. I’ve also asked ops to pull staging hostnames from the telemetry.

I’ll update you by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Invoice 2026-04 — token attribution check (prelim results)

Hi Samantha — I pulled a preliminary usage slice for your org between 2026-04-14 and 2026-04-16. Attached is a redacted CSV with the top 50 prefixes and a small staging-log-snippet.

Prelim findings:
- ~312,214 tokens billed to your org in that window attributable to API keys that were flagged as non-prod by our heuristics (hostnames matching "staging." and user_agent tags from your integration tests).
- Our billing pipeline currently attributes tokens to the top-level org tied to the API key. We do not automatically exclude keys unless they have the "exclude_from_billing" tag applied.

Options we propose:
1) Credit: We can issue a retroactive credit for tokens with the staging hostnames once you confirm the request ids. Credit would appear as a line-item on next invoice (or we can apply a prepayment credit now if you prefer faster reconciliation).
2) Tagging: We can help you add a key-level tag to exclude future keys from billing (recommended).
3) VAT: If your VAT id validates and reverse-charge applies, we will reissue the invoice net of VAT.

Next steps: Please send the three full request ids you mentioned and confirm whether you want a credit applied immediately or on next invoice.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Billing Operations Specialist
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Invoice 2026-04 — resolution plan and next steps

Samantha — gracias, and thanks for the quick data. Summary / next steps from Redwood: 

1) Attribution check: Lauren’s team matched the three request ids you sent to entries in our token store and confirmed they were billed to the Cartwheel org. We’ll attach the per-request token counts to the credit memo. Sample line for your requests: 3f7a9b8c-1a2b-4c9d-8e5e-4c9bfb2a7c01 — 5,120 tokens.

2) Credit: We will issue a retroactive credit for all tokens flagged with staging hostnames in that window (~312,214 tokens). The credit will be visible as a separate line on your May invoice (Redwood-2026-05) and will reduce the payable amount accordingly. Since you requested payment hold, please keep April payment on hold for the disputed portion; outstanding non-disputed lines are still owed.

3) VAT: We validated DE123456789 against VIES and confirm you are eligible for reverse-charge. We will reissue net invoice (no VAT) and provide a VAT-stamped invoice copy simultaneously with the credit memo.

4) Sampling / telemetry: Our billing extraction is deterministic for the last 30 days and we do not sample for monthly billing windows. We will export per-request token counts for all matched request ids and include a short telemetry audit CSV in the credit memo packet.

5) Prevent recurrence: Ben will coordinate with your integrations lead to add an "exclude_from_billing" tag to CI keys and help you configure hostname-based exclusion on the Redwood routing layer. Action owner: Ben Carter (sales engineering) to run a 30‑minute call next week.

I’ll follow up with the credit memo + reissued invoice by COB Friday. If you prefer the credit applied immediately as an account prepayment, tell us and Lauren will action it.

Thanks again for flagging this early — we’ll get it sorted and provide the export for your audit.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference
